newsitem.title: USA: Oakley sees Q3 EPS exceeding estimates.
newsitem.headline: Oakley sees Q3 EPS exceeding estimates.

text.p: Oakley Inc, whose stock price fell more than 10 percent on Thursday, said Friday it expects third quarter earnings to exceed analysts' estimates of about $0.41 a share.
Oakley shares tumbled over seven points to close at 37-1/4 on Thursday, hurt by Sunglass Hut International Inc's forecast of weak third quarter profits.
Oakley Chief Financial Officer Link Newcomb said, "In spite of events at Sunglass Hut, we understand that sales of Oakley products in their stores have remained strong.
"In addition, we are excited about our new product introductions, which are on schedule for the balance of the year."

The Irvine, Calif., company said that in the first half, sales to Sunglass Hut represented about one-third of Oakley's total net sales. "There has been no fundamental changes in the company or its business," Oakley said.
The company plans to announce full financial results for the third quarter on October 17.
At September 30, its backlog of orders was about $19.3 million (adjusted for Sunglass Hut order reductions received by the company to date). Backorders were about $1.6 million.
A year earlier, the backlog was $15.6 million and backorders were $5.6 million.
On Thursday, Sunglass Hut shares tumbled almost 32 percent after the company's earnings warning, and the stock was downgraded by Alex. Brown & Sons and Morgan Stanley.
